title: What an explicit scene earns
verbatim: B, and joy may stand. B by default, and a settled pair may have a night that is only pleasure and warmth, its consequence small: a habit, a mark, a witness.
question: Beyond Rule 9's consequence afterward, what must every explicit scene do for the story?

title: On the page or cut
verbatim: Always on the page. Any sex that happens inside a scene is written explicitly, start to finish, with no cut and no fade; the aftermath follows on the page.
question: May an explicit scene ever cut away before the act, to the morning or the next scene?

title: When the first time comes
verbatim: When the people would. No pacing rule: NPCs act on their wants and refusal lines, so sex may come first and the bond after, or never. Table Rule 3 decides.
question: Across a thread, when does a pair's first explicit scene arrive?

title: The lover's desire and refusal
verbatim: Desire, refusal, and the hinge. As B, plus a third field: what would change their mind, either way. Rule 9's change of mind then has a planted cause a player can find.
question: Where does a lover's own desire and refusal line live, and what does it hold?

title: What the Ledger keeps
verbatim: Yes to: Debts and promises (Whatever was promised, owed, bargained or betrayed in bed is entered and comes due like any other debt); Witnesses and reputation (Who heard, who saw, who will talk: gossip, scandal and a rival's leverage, entered as who-saw-what, and able to open a Front); Marks on the body (Bites, bruises, beard-burn, a strained hip, another's scent on the skin: entered and carried on real healing times (R60-02), visible to whoever looks); What was learned (A secret told, a scar seen, a weakness found in bed is entered as knowledge the other now holds, and may use).
question: After an intimate scene, which consequences go on the Ledger and persist?

title: The words, by culture
verbatim: Crude English, native in mouths. Narration keeps one crude English; each culture's own words for the body arrive in speech and italic thought, as its swears do.
question: Are the plain words for the body one crude English in every POV, or does each culture carry its own?

title: How long it runs
verbatim: By weight. A first time, a turning point or a dark scene runs as a set piece; a returning pair's night inside a chapter runs on that chapter's length, the aftermath always written.
question: In a written scene or chapter, how long does an explicit scene run?

title: Tracking the bodies
verbatim: Fixed at each new pose. Each new arrangement is fixed in one clear sentence as it forms; between poses, sensation leads and the geometry may blur. This settles the two skills' wording.
question: How closely does the page track where the bodies are?

title: Which sense leads
verbatim: The POV's own order. The POV's body and trade decide: a beastkin nose first, a Moto eye first, a sealer's hands first. Rule 9's scents still appear in every scene.
question: In an explicit scene, which sense leads the layering?

title: Talk in bed
verbatim: Full voice, talk as play. Each partner talks in bed the way their card talks out of it, crude, teasing, bargaining or tender, and the talk is part of the act.
question: How much talk does an explicit scene carry, and what kind?

title: Power games, framed
verbatim: By each culture's form. The Accord seals terms on paper, the Moto enter a word in form, Kharven takes a word before witnesses; the stop-word carries that culture's weight, and breaking it is answered under that culture's own law (R53-11).
question: When lovers play at power (binding, command, pain by agreement), how is the game framed in the world?

title: Consent on the page
verbatim: Both, read together. Words and body both carry it. A refusal in either channel is a refusal; where the two disagree the scene has become dubcon (dubious consent) and is written as dubcon (SC9).
question: How does consent show in an explicit scene: in words, in the body, or both?

title: Reading a lover
verbatim: Senses free, workings by leave. What cannot shut, a beastkin nose or ears, reads freely; a worked read, by Gnosis or a Moto's eyes, needs leave, and one taken unasked is B's trespass, with B's tell, counter and debt.
question: When a lover can read the other by faculty, nose or eye, may that read run in bed without leave?

title: Workings on desire
verbatim: Desire, with tell and counter. An Obsession or Attraction working, a charm or a Draft may make someone want; it shows a tell, has a findable counter, costs its user, and the aftermath knows it was made.
question: May a working, a charm or a Draft create desire or bend consent on the page?

title: Bedchamber arts
verbatim: Given or drawn, fully priced. A bedchamber art is a technique: a Codex line, a cost in both bodies, a tell, a counter, no figure until canon holds one. One drawing unasked is a Claim, and the scene dubcon or non-con (SC8).
question: May the act itself carry a working, Essence given, pooled or drawn between the partners?

title: The body under coercion
verbatim: Shown, known as reflex. Arousal may be written, and the POV knows it for the body's reflex, apart from her will; she carries that knowledge into the aftermath.
question: In a dubcon or non-con scene, may the victim's body respond with arousal on the page, and how is it framed?

title: Carrying it forward
verbatim: Yes to: In the body and habit (The survivor's later scenes carry it physically (the startle, sleep that will not come, the seat with its back to the wall) until the thread resolves it); The bill reaches the world (The act opens or advances a Front: feud, blood-debt, pregnancy, scandal or a case at law; the perpetrator's own account is a lie in his mouth (Rule 8)).
question: After a non-con or coerced scene, how does it carry into later scenes?

title: The aftermath beat
verbatim: Procedure, meaning unsaid. The aftermath is the small work after (washing, the fire fed, clothes found, the door), and neither partner says what it meant; the change shows in how they do it.
question: What shape does the aftermath of an explicit scene take on the page?

title: Your character in the bed
verbatim: Contact as world fact. Once your post sets the act, contact, position and what the partner does to him are world facts; his arousal, pleasure, pain and climax, and how he bears them, stay yours.
question: In a roleplay turn, what may Natalie write of your character's body during an explicit scene?

title: The explicit roleplay turn
verbatim: Standing orders in bed. You may post the course of the encounter, a pace, a limit or a stop for your character, and Natalie runs it to the first branch it does not cover, then stops there.
question: How does a full roleplay turn run when the scene in it is explicit?

title: An NPC who would force him
verbatim: Threat placed, his post decides. Natalie sets the threat in the room (the grip, the bargain, the Draft in the cup) and stops; the act reaches the page only through your post.
question: If an NPC would coerce or force your character, how far does the turn go?

title: Where courtship custom lives
verbatim: Courtship field, plus mores. A, plus a Mores field: what the culture holds shameful and what it boasts of, nakedness and bathing, the pleasure trade (CO18), and what its law does to adultery and to rape, written beside R70-45's law field.
question: Where does each culture's courtship and marriage custom live?

title: Kharven courtship
verbatim: Yes to: The stack proves him (A suitor splits for her household's woodpile unasked, labour-debt run in reverse; the asking comes when the stack is full and her kin say so. Entered in the Kharven field); The skin answers (Her household answers at the hearth: she drinks from the sealskin and passes it across the fire, and he drinks after her before everyone. A withheld skin is the no, said without a word); Ridden off, priced after (On the nameless day a man may ride off with a woman, and her kin name a price on the first named morning. Whether she went willing is hers to tell; the custom never asks).
question: Which customs make a Kharven match?

title: Moto courtship
verbatim: Yes to: Asked in form, entered (A match is asked in form at the hinge of the day and is real only when the register holds it in the house's own hand; an unentered lover is nobody to the house); The eyes offered (A suitor outside the line courts by lifting his eyes to a Moto and leaving them there, offering himself to be read; whether she reads him, and how far, is her answer).
question: Which customs make a Moto match?

title: Accord courtship
verbatim: Yes to: Terms under seal (A match is a settlement drawn by an advocate, pledged 'Ita spondeo' and entered in ink, with what stays in her name written in. Courtship is the negotiation, and love shows in the clauses); Breach of promise sued (A broken engagement is actionable at the Assize: the letters are read aloud in open court and the Bench prices the jilt. Every love letter in the Accord is also evidence).
question: Which customs make an Accord match?

title: Mahuo courtship
verbatim: Yes to: A sijo owed a sijo (Courtship is a verse exchange: the suitor's three lines are answered with three, and the last clause turns. A plain answer costs standing, as R70-110 rules at court); The speech level drops (The proposal is a change of speech: one of them drops from the high forms to the plain speech kept for kin and spouses, and the other answering in kind is the yes).
question: Which customs make a Mahuo match?

title: Courtship in the lineage halls
verbatim: Yes to: Entered in the book (A marriage is real when the husband's hall enters her in its book as 'of' her father's hall; a secondary wife is entered lower, and an unentered woman has no standing in the hall); Bought for the book (A hall marries for a skill it lacks, and the bride-gifts come with a schedule of what her children will be taught. Love is a clause, and the halls say so).
question: Which customs make a match in the lineage halls?

title: Dawi courtship
verbatim: Yes to: Entered, never promised (A Dawi match is made backward: the acts already done for each other are entered in the Tally in metre, and the entry is the marriage. There is no betrothal); Kurlo, the refusal unsaid (Courtship is 'Kurlo' said alone between two people, with the 'Ei kurme' that would end a bargain left off: a thing unbegun and not refused, the nearest the tongue comes to hope).
question: Which customs make a Dawi match?

title: Consorts, concubines, widows
verbatim: Yes to: Entered lower, in book (The lineage halls and the Moto enter a secondary wife or consort below the wife in the book or register; her children's standing is written there, and an unentered child is 'written in the wrong hand'); Accord: off the books (One spouse in Accord law. A kept woman or kept man lives on an allowance quoted from the price table, a scandal with a sum on it, and their children are sine sigillo); Kharven: the brother's widow (A Kharven widow and her stack may pass to her dead man's brother, wife or no wife, if she takes the skin from him, so no hearth goes cold; refusing is her right, and her hunger); Dawi: one entry only (The Tally holds one marriage entry. A second partner is an act nobody will stand behind, 'kurnur', unentered, and carries that swear in the hold).
question: Which marriage laws beyond one spouse for life go into the Inventories?

title: The pleasure trade
verbatim: Each culture's own form. The Accord licenses houses under seal and inspection, Eastern courts keep ranked quarters or verse-trained entertainers, the north keeps no house and trades in kind; entered in CO1's Mores field, fees as price-table rows on your word.
question: Does the Draw Age keep a trade in sex on the page, and in what form?

title: Marriage as politics
verbatim: A Front with a clock. A political match in play runs as a Front: betrothal, settlement, wedding and first heir are its ticks. A broken match fires the Front, and someone pays.
question: When a match is political, how does the table run it?

title: Jealousy and rivals
verbatim: Yes to: A feud with a bill (Jealousy acts: slander, theft, a duel, poison. Each act lands on the Ledger as a debt or a witness, and a love rival who recurs is paid for as R70-104 rules); The road to Obsession (Fed long enough, jealousy turns to Obsession Force: Breadth collapses and Empathy runs one way. An instrument or a good Gnosis read can find it, which is its fair counter).
question: What does jealousy do in WOTR?

title: Conception and the pox
verbatim: Ruled openly, every time. Each bed between partners who could conceive records its precaution (sheath, sponge, timing, a Draft, or none) in the notes; Natalie rules conception and the pox by period medicine, names what decided, and a pregnancy opens a Front.
question: Do conception and the pox ride on every bed?

title: Love across a Stage gap
verbatim: Yes to: He holds it, and pays (The higher partner suppresses at home every waking hour; his jaw, collar and temper carry it, and the household learns to read the bill); Drawn off by an art (A partner who holds a draining art, as Yorime does, may take the Pressure off by touch at that art's own price, traced to Fracture of Worlds before first use; love alone draws nothing).
question: What does a Stage gap cost a couple over the years?

title: Pressure in bed
verbatim: Let go, by leave. A, plus: a lover may ask him to stop holding it in. Letting go is the most intimate thing a practitioner can give, and she pays in sweat and nausea she chose.
question: Can Pressure reach desire in bed?

title: Lovers and the warm bond
verbatim: Never the only one. Lovers count, but each thread also keeps a warm bond that is not romantic, so a romance that dies, sours or turns to Obsession leaves warmth standing.
question: Does a romance count as a thread's standing warm bond?

title: How a bond grows
verbatim: Yes to: Tokens and maintenance (A bond grows by what is mended, fed and carried: the coat, the comb, the bowl. Each scene adds one, and the reader counts them); Jeong through hardship (A bond grows from shared cost, chosen or not: a night in a collapsed gallery, a winter of short rations. Enemies can accrue it, and it binds them anyway); Crystal fact, no figure (The breakthrough readout R70-84 already owes at Flourishing also names its Catalyst, the first Spirit Axis, with no figure (R12-5); no other bond prints, and nothing says whether she loves him).
question: How does a bond show itself growing across scenes?

title: Love mourned or lived
verbatim: Lived first, then cost. A bond gets scenes of its own joy before a loss may land on it; a love that dies before the reader has seen it lived is a fault to fix.
question: How much of WOTR's love is lived before it is lost?

title: A bond after death
verbatim: Clean or a cage. A, plus the turn: grief fed long enough tips the bond into Obsession, which an instrument or a good Gnosis read can find, and a Crystal grown dependent on the dead risks FOW's fracture events.
question: What does a lover's death do to the survivor's Crystal?

title: Where the intimacy law lands
verbatim: B, plus the Inventories. B, plus the courtship and mores fields drafted for the six cultures from these answers and entered on your word, and an intimacy section in the Dialogue Craft Standards and Scene Writing Process Guide.
question: How do your intimacy answers land in the repo?

title: Intimacy checks in verify_scene
verbatim: Yes to: An explicit mode (verify --explicit WARNs on a scene with no smell word, no sound or mimetic word, an italic mimetic word, or notes without a consequence line, and stops counting 'cock' as gun vocabulary); A floor guard (FAIL when an explicit scene names anyone whose card or roster gives an age under eighteen; WARN when a named partner has no age on file. The body's age counts, never a soul's); Euphemism bans (Bed euphemisms that dodge R49-51 (his member, her sex, manhood, her core) FAIL in narration like the hard-ban words; in a mouth they pass, since a character may be coy); Stale-touch watch (WARN past one a scene on the archive's repeated touches: the hand on the arm, the jaw held, the kiss on the hair, as R71-103 does for fight devices).
question: Which checks should verify_scene gain with this law?

title: The intimacy sample bank
verbatim: Both. A and B: culture beats where Natalie already loads them, and the kinds the archive lacks; this questionnaire's samples become their first drafts.
question: What should the intimacy sample bank hold?

title: Proof and the test scene
verbatim: Law, checks, NPC test. Log the law and build ME2's checks; write one explicit scene between adult NPCs on your thread's Kharven ground, a Kharven half and a Moto half split by a break mark (R49-27); amend; then guides, Inventories and bank.
question: In what order does the work run, and who is in the test scene?
